lanes.objective: TASKS.md row task_945 (GATE-05) makes TWO separate claims about check_no_inert_ssot_tables: that it 'credits a table from prose', and that it 'cannot tell a sub-table read from a top-level one'. MEASURE BOTH, they can come out differently. (1) Locate the check and quote its predicate with path:line. (2) 'Credits a table from prose' means the check counts a mios.toml table as live because its NAME APPEARS SOMEWHERE -- in a comment, a doc, a string -- rather than because code reads it. That is SKILL.md section 7's Measuring the Wrong Property: prove it by naming a table the check currently credits and showing the only occurrence is non-code, or refute it by showing the predicate requires a real read. (3) 'Cannot tell a sub-table from a top-level one' means [a.b] is credited when only [a] is read, or the reverse; demonstrate with a specific table pair from mios.toml. (4) Construct the violation the check should catch -- a genuinely inert table -- IN YOUR WORKTREE ONLY, run the check, and report whether it stays green. RESTORE the tree; your findings file is the only change you leave. Do NOT fix it. Write .devloop/findings/task_945.md in the required section layout, with the count of tables the check credits versus the count it would credit under a read-only predicate in NUMBERS. Re-derive it yourself, then OVERWRITE that file with your own finding and state in WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE whether you reproduced the earlier verdict or overturned it, and on what evidence. Run every command in the FOREGROUND and wait for its exit code; if you use run_command, set WaitMsBeforeAsync high enough to cover the command rather than letting it default.
